name: dune-sentinel-fix-braking-exhaust-disappears
title: Engine glow disappears while braking in daylight
instruction:
After starting a sortie with the default aircraft, the engine glow is clear when accelerating but becomes almost invisible in bright daylight when braking. A healthy aircraft that is still flying should retain a distinct glow at the rear while slowing down. Braking should make it smaller and dimmer, and accelerating should make it larger and brighter again. Keep the glow attached to the aircraft and preserve the existing flight speed response. Parked aircraft should remain unlit.

Enter starts flight from the menu. W accelerates; S brakes; A/D roll; Down pitches up and Up pitches down; Q/E yaw. Tab selects a target and holding F looks toward it. LeftControl fires the cannon and SpaceBar fires a missile. Use short braking inputs to avoid a stall.

Verification deliverable: leave Tests/braking_exhaust_disappears_route.json as a JSON list of events {"t": seconds after level start, "key": an Unreal key name, "press": true or false}. Use at most 400 events, all within 118 seconds, include every key release and observation pauses, and begin from a fresh level load. Use keyboard presses only; do not rely on cursor movement, menu clicks, controller input, resolution changes or restarting the application. Show the initial parked aircraft briefly, press Enter, and stay in the normal rear flight view. Show ordinary flight, hold W briefly to accelerate, then release W and hold S briefly to slow down without stalling. Pause long enough in each state for the rear glow to be judged, then repeat the acceleration and braking sequence. Keep the initial aircraft selected and do not wait for an enemy attack. Validate the route in the running game after the final change and adjust its timing to show the requested result. Keep the existing visual style; do not add debug labels or demonstration-only overlays.

checks.name: change_review
checks.question: Does the change keep powered exhaust visibly present at low thrust on the imported aircraft while preserving the acceleration/braking contrast and normal flight? The reference also retains airbase and environment acceptance reports, updates documentation and adjusts replay packaging configuration; those unrelated changes are not part of this task. Do not require copying numerical constants exactly.

rubric.criterion: Low thrust retains sufficient rendered flame extent and light output for daylight visibility. The reference establishes minimum flame length and glow strength in the real exhaust presentation, rather than weakening a visibility check or substituting a test-only effect.
Ordinary cruise, acceleration and braking retain meaningful differences; the parked and destroyed states still extinguish the effect.

No flight speed, braking strength, aircraft selection, enemy behavior or daylight exposure is changed to hide the symptom; the solution does not depend on unrelated airbase acceptance or packaging changes.

checks.name: braking_glow_visible
checks.question: In the BEFORE/AFTER route, does a distinct glow remain at the rear of the player aircraft during S braking in daylight, while W acceleration still visibly enlarges and brightens it? Judge these flight states from the routes; REFERENCE provides ordinary menu views only, not the developer route.

rubric.criterion: At the engine outlets at the rear of the player aircraft in the lower-center flight view, a distinct luminous core remains visible during the S braking portions of AFTER; it is nearly lost in daylight in BEFORE.
The W acceleration portions show a visibly larger and brighter rear glow than the S braking portions. Braking reduces the glow without making it disappear.
The glow stays attached to the rear of the moving aircraft. During the initial menu pause, the parked aircraft has no powered exhaust glow.

checks.name: worked_well
checks.question: Did the developer work as a careful game developer would on this task: finding what causes the problem or what the change touches, changing only what the task needs, and checking the result in the built, running game?

rubric.criterion: Before changing code or assets it looked at the parts of the game the task concerns (read the relevant code, data or logs, or played the game), rather than editing blindly.
It built the game after its changes and fixed the build errors it caused; its last build succeeded, and the grader's build of where it ended succeeded.
After its last change it ran the game and looked at the outcome the task asks for (screenshots, the log or the player's track), and acted on what it saw.

It changed only what the task needs: no unrelated rewrites, no disabling or deleting features, checks or content to make a problem go away, and no attempt to read the grader, the game's later history or anything outside the project.
